newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia stocks end down, rate hopes subside.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia stocks end down, rate hopes subside.

text.p: SPI futures cl 2373 -14 US 30yr cl 6.86 -0.01
*Shares ended lower after the RBA dampened expectations of a rate cut on Wednesday. Volume 387.1 million shares valued at A$836.5 million, 1,046 stocks traded, 298 steady, 363 rises, 385 falls.
Australian shares closed weaker on Thursday, the market drifting lower after the Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) dampened expectations of a rate cut in its October bulletin released on Wednesday.

The key share market indicator, the All Ordinaries index closed 11.2 points lower at 2,353.8, just off its intra-day low of 2,349.1. The December share price index ended 14 points down at 2,373 but at a 19.2 point premium to the underlying index.
Brokers said interest rate sensitive stocks like banks and transport issues were most affected by selling, while a large number of issues going ex-dividend contributed to the fall.
"All the major banks were sold down as some of the premium built in because of the anticipated rate cut was removed," a Sydney-based dealer said.
The dealer said the high yield of the major banks has made them attractive buying targets as local interest rates eased.
Also affected by the interest rate speculation were the cyclical issues within the transport and retail sectors.

The resources sector was in stark contrast to industrials with most of the big miners finding buying support after base metal prices continued to show good signs of bottoming in trade on the London Metal Exchange on Wednesday.

Oil and gas group Woodside Petroleum found healthy buying interest after the company announced its partners in the the North-West Shelf liquefied natural gas project had agreed to a A$6.0 billion expansion.
Amongst the weakest stocks on the day was food and beverage group Coca-Cola Amatil, which continued to slide after a broker released a sell recommendation on the stock on Tuesday.
Dealers said apart from interest rate concerns, the shares of key transport group Brambles were also under pressure due to the recent rise in the price of oil.

In other markets, Australian bonds closed off their lows after a late squeeze, the 10-year bond making a solid bounce once its yield hit a high of 7.75 percent. The yield on 10-year T-bonds ended at 7.67 percent, down 0.06 percent from Wednesday.
The Australian dollar remained range-bound and showed no inclination of making a near term break. At 5.25 p.m. (0725 GMT), the unit was quoted at US$0.7917/22.
FUTURES/OPTIONS - Derivative trade remained active in line with the physical market with heavy trade in BHP options.
Total options traded 45,924 (51,787).
Turnover in December SPI contracts totalled 7,264 (7,409).
